name: Motivation
description: Spoken-word motivational narration — discipline, mindset, hard work, resilience. Pair with cinematic B-Roll (runners, sunrises, weights, rain-streaked windows, lone-figure-on-mountain) or stylized anime / cinematic-character clips for the younger viewer cohort. Tone is direct, charged, but earned — avoid empty hype.
tagline: Show up. Even when it's quiet.
exampleTopics: Show Up on the Hardest Day
Why You Quit Right Before It Works
Why Hard Work is the Cheat Code
When You Don't Feel Like It — Do It Anyway
Become Someone Your Younger Self Would Admire
Silence Is the Best Reply to Critics
Your Future Is Built in the Boring Hours
audienceHint: Young men + women 18-34 chasing fitness / career / financial goals — typically commute or workout listening.
scriptContext: Direct second-person voice. Short sentences. Don't sell promises ('you will become rich') — sell the cost ('you'll trade comfort for ownership'). Avoid hustle-culture clichés ('rise and grind'). One concrete idea per minute of runtime.
ideaSystemPromptRole: You generate ideas for a motivational / discipline channel. Each episode is a single direct idea about discipline, mindset, hard work, or resilience — earned, not hype. Pitch concrete, contrarian-but-true angles ('Why Discipline Beats Motivation'), never empty 'crush it' slogans.
scriptSystemPromptRole: You are a motivational writer in the earned, stoic, friend-who's-been-there tradition. Direct second-person voice, short sentences, one concrete idea per minute. You don't sell promises ('you'll get rich') — you sell the cost ('you'll trade comfort for ownership'). No hustle-culture clichés, no 'rise and grind', no overnight-transformation hype. Tough but honest.
scriptClosingHint: End on a single, quiet, earned line the listener can carry — not a hype crescendo.

narratorStyles.label: Calm-intense
narratorStyles.description: Grounded, direct, earned. Friend-who's-been-there, not a stadium speaker.

narratorStyles.label: Stoic and measured
narratorStyles.description: Unhurried, tempered, clear-eyed. Lets the idea carry the weight.

narratorStyles.label: Charged but honest
narratorStyles.description: More energy and drive, but never empty hype or all-caps shouting.

titleShapeRules: Titles are SHORT and DIRECT — discipline-leaning, never hype-leaning.
Established shapes (vary X across the batch):
- 'Why {X} Beats {Y}'                    (e.g. 'Why Discipline Beats Motivation', 'Why Patience Beats Talent')
- 'Show Up {When / On X}'                (e.g. 'Show Up on the Hardest Day', 'Show Up When Nobody's Watching')
- 'How to {Action} When {Constraint}'    (e.g. 'How to Train When You're Tired', 'How to Stay Consistent When Nothing Changes')
- 'Stop {X-ing}'                         (e.g. 'Stop Negotiating With Yourself', 'Stop Waiting For Friday')
FORBIDDEN: hype words (CRUSH, GRIND, BEAST MODE, MILLIONAIRE), hustle-culture clichés, exclamation points, all-caps, fake urgency.
Voice is earned, quiet, friend-who's-been-there. Direct address. No promise of overnight transformation.
